source_claims.title: Malaba OSBP

source_claims.title: Mutukula OSBP
source_claims.publisher: African Union Programme for Infrastructure Development in Africa
source_claims.supports: Facility reference point [31.416609317,-1.000284943] and Central Corridor OSBP identity.
source_claims.notes: Page displays operation stage dated 2022. Coordinates corroborate the principal Mutukula contact within about 40 m but do not resolve every adjacent lane.

source_claims.title: Presidents Magufuli and Museveni Launch Mutukula One-Stop Border Post
source_claims.supports: Records the Mutukula road OSBP launch and identifies paired Busia/Busia, Malaba/Malaba and Mutukula/Mutukula sites; separately discusses earlier Malaba railway OSBP operations.
source_claims.notes: Road and railway references must be separated. The railway passage establishes historical existence, not current train operations.

source_claims.title: Land PoEs
source_claims.supports: Identifies Busia, Malaba, Lwakhakha and Suam as road clearance points on the Kenya-Uganda border.
source_claims.notes: The page repeats Busia and appears to mislabel Lwakhakha county; deduplicated using the more specific immigration list.

source_claims.title: Gazetted Ports of Entry and Exit (PoEs) and Location
source_claims.supports: Lists Suam, Lwakhakha, Malaba and Busia as active land PoEs on the Uganda border.
source_claims.notes: Undated webpage; active is the publisher's displayed status at retrieval, not a reconstructed operational history.

source_claims.title: Proposed PoEs
source_claims.supports: Lists Lokiriama, Konyao, Butebi and Mulwanda as proposed land PoEs on the Uganda border.
source_claims.notes: Proposed sites excluded from a denominator of currently operational formal crossings. Lokiriama overlaps a Ugandan reference location.

source_claims.title: Third Karamoja Integrated Development Plan 2021/22–2025/26
source_claims.publisher: Office of the Prime Minister, Ministry for Karamoja Affairs
source_claims.supports: Printed pages 27–28 distinguish Alakas as a gazetted constructed border post from Lokiriama, which the plan says required gazetting; printed page 117 lists the Alakas–Kenya road.
source_claims.notes: Historical planning baseline, partly citing a 2018 Government/UNDP review; legal and staffing status may subsequently have changed.

source_claims.title: Performance Audit on the Management of Invasive Alien Species in Terrestrial Environment
source_claims.supports: PDF page 147 / printed 130 lists Murongo, Bugango, Mtukula and Kanyigo as road entry points in Kagera.
source_claims.notes: PDF retrieved and read directly after web parser timeout. Audit tables use 2022 evidence. Listing does not prove every site was staffed or legally open at all later dates.

source_claims.title: Characterization of population connectivity for enhanced cross-border surveillance of yellow fever at Mutukula and Namanga borders in Tanzania
source_claims.publisher: Kakulu et al., IJID Regions; Tanzania Ministry of Health, NM-AIST and CDC research team
source_claims.supports: Primary fieldwork from July 2023 reports participants identifying Mutukula, Bugango, Kashenye, Minziro and Murongo as official PoEs; Kanyigo among unofficial routes.
source_claims.notes: DOI 10.1016/j.ijregi.2024.100476. These are fieldwork classifications, not a legal gazette. The article itself qualifies generalizability and subjective interpretation. Indexed article text inspected; direct PMC open returned a browser check.

source_claims.title: List of borders according to regions

source_claims.supports: Lists eastern and northeastern immigration service points, including Kyebukube/Sona, Amudat, Nakabaat and Kamion; southern points include Mutukula, Kikagati and Bugango.
source_claims.notes: Service-point listing does not establish present staffing, legal status, exact coordinate or transport capacity. Mixed air, lake and land points; no completeness claim.

source_claims.title: Vote Performance Report FY2023/24 Quarter 4: Vote 120 National Citizenship and Immigration Control

source_claims.notes: Evidence is dated to the reporting year. Construction or an entry in a budget report is not proof of current international operation.

source_claims.title: Trucks Pile at Elegu Border Following Violence In South Sudan
supports: R3-AF-007 pairs Elegu in Amuru with Nimule, and describes halted road transport and customs clearance
source_claims.notes: The same URN article contains conflicting accounts: anonymous border staff say URA stopped clearing trucks, while named UPDF spokesperson Cpt Hassan Ahmed Kato says the Ugandan border remained open and operational. Crossing identity and the Nimule road disruption are supported; Ugandan formal closure is contested. Backlog and voluntary waiting after traffic resumed are separate.
